summary: Concordia Venus is a card-driven economic game about building trade networks across the Roman map, using a hand of role cards that get better as you buy more of them. It's calm and cerebral, with victory hinging on a hidden multiplier formula few players see coming until the reveal.
criticised: scoring formula (Prefects/multipliers) is hard to plan around for newcomers
can feel a bit dry or thinky for non-Euro fans
map choice greatly affects strategy leading to snowbally openings
some find the theme thin dressing on a mechanism

interaction.kind: parallel economic building with light space competition
interaction.detail: Players build on a shared map and can be blocked from settling certain cities first, but most of the game is independent engine-building on your own tableau of cards. Interaction is indirect, coming from racing for the same city slots and resource availability rather than direct attacks.

subsystems: resource-type multiplier scoring (brick, food, tools, wine, cloth production cards)
sources: Vis cards multiplying owned production buildings per good
scoring.how_you_win: You spend the game building production buildings and buying multiplier cards for the five goods; once a player exhausts their colonists/cards the end is triggered, and everyone then totals goods-multiplier VP plus the Prefect city bonus, highest wins.
